title: Support Toolsmith Bridgelet and Fallback Heuristics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: On-call engineers and support staff regularly run short operational snippets (checks, fixes, rollbacks) that are stored as curated text in the admin snippets catalog. Running those snippets ad-hoc is error-prone (missing context, unsafe side-effects) and hard to audit. We need a small bridge service — Toolsmith Bridgelet — that converts vetted snippets into safe, callable micro-tasks with built-in idempotency, automatic fallback heuristics, and telemetry so first-line responders can execute reliably and engineers can observe and remediate regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Bridgelet exposes a stable HTTP API to create and invoke snippet-based tasks (POST /v1/tasks, POST /v1/tasks/:id/invoke)
Each created task receives an idempotency token and persisted input snapshot in the tasks DB

Fallback heuristic triggers when a task invocation hits either (a) external dependency timeout or (b) failure-pattern matched in the first N logs — the bridgelet should route to a safe fallback variant if present
Execution traces, inputs, outputs, and fallback activations are emitted to ops-telemetry with schema op.task.invoke.v1
E2E smoke tests exercising normal execution, timeout-based fallback, and manual rollback all pass in CI
RBAC checks and audit entries are recorded for every task invocation (console UI shows user and route)
Canary rollout for 10% of traffic over 72 hours with SLOs observed (error rate < 0.5%, median latency < 250ms for quick checks)
design_decisions: Persist tasks in a lightweight Postgres table (tasks.id, snippet_id, inputs_json, idempotency_key, status, created_by, created_at, logs_link)
Use existing admin snippets catalog as canonical source; bridgelet cannot alter snippet content — only wrap it in execution metadata
Fallback variants are user-provided optional snippets referenced by metadata (snippet.fallbacks) and treated as lower-privilege operations
Execution sandboxing: run short snippets via the ops-runlet execution service (already available) with execution-level timeouts and capped permissions
Telemetry schema chosen to align with ops-telemetry v2: include fields service, snippet_id, task_id, invocation_id, outcome, fallback_used, duration_ms
Authentication: require token with scope task:invoke; integrate with SSO and include user identity in audit events
implementation_notes: - POST /v1/tasks => create task wrapper from snippet_id and inputs; returns task_id and idempotency_key
- POST /v1/tasks/:task_id/invoke => starts invocation with user identity header; enqueues to runlet; returns invocation_id
- GET /v1/tasks/:task_id/status => current status and recent logs link

Data flow: API -> validate RBAC -> write task row -> enqueue to runlet -> runlet executes snippet -> bridgelet listens for result and evaluates fallback policy -> if fallback, enqueue fallback snippet and emit fallback telemetry

Fallback policy evaluation logic (pseudo): check for any runlet timeout OR if runlet logs contain regex patterns from false-positive whitelist; only fire fallback if fallback snippet exists and is marked safe
Idempotency: client-provided optional idempotency_key; bridgelet dedupes on (snippet_id, idempotency_key, user) for 24h window and returns previous invocation_id if deduped
Observability: emit traces to X-Ray-compatible tracing and metrics to prometheus (histogram for duration, counter for fallback activations)
Safety gate: any snippet that alters production state must have at least one owner and a recent approval flag in snippet metadata; otherwise invocation is blocked in the bridgelet
Testing: add unit tests for fallback matcher, integration test against runlet sandbox, and a mutation test asserting idempotency dedupe
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): feature branch + local runlet simulator + unit tests; demo to oncall in staging
Phase 2 (internal canary): deploy to staging and enable for 2 internal teams (oncall + platform) for 2 weeks; collect telemetry and iterate
Phase 3 (controlled prod canary): route 10% of create/invoke calls to bridgelet for 72 hours; monitor metrics: fallback_rate, invocation_error_rate, median_latency, manual_intervention_count
Phase 4 (GA): enable for all internal teams with UI affordances in Console and add runbook documentation
Rollback criteria: sustained invocation_error_rate > 1% for 12 hours OR increase in manual_intervention_count by > 200% vs baseline
risks_mitigation: Risk: fallback snippet could cause broader impact — Mitigation: require fallback ownership and mark fallback snippets as read-only in admin catalog
Risk: false positives trigger fallback too aggressively — Mitigation: expose a safety-threshold config and start with conservative matchers; log near-miss cases for tuning
Risk: audit gap if bridgelet crashes mid-invocation — Mitigation: write pre-invoke audit row before enqueue and update on completion; use at-least-once semantics to avoid lost audit events
Risk: performance overhead — Mitigation: optimize hot path for quick checks and use a small in-memory LRU cache for snippet metadata
tasks: Proto: implement API surface and task model (week 1)
Engine: integrate with runlet and implement fallback evaluator (week 2)
Telemetry: emit events and dashboards; add alerts (week 3)
QA: E2E tests, failure-mode tests, and chaos injections (week 4)
Docs + Console: add invocation history UI and quickstart guide (week 5)
Canary: rollout and monitor; address issues and GA (week 6)
Post-GA: collect usage patterns and propose batching/optimization follow-ups
